summary: Bong Seok Joo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed undergraduate studies at UC Berkeley under Lewis Lancaster, Ding-hwa E. Hsieh, and Morio Hamada, and earned a PhD at Princeton under Stephen F. Teiser, Jacqueline I. Stone, and Yang Lu.

Bongkil Chung is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at Michigan State University under George C. Kerner. He served on the faculty at Florida International University from 1991 to 1992, where he was attested as professor of philosophy in 2012.

Borayin Larios specializes in Indology and religious studies. Educated at Freiburg (MA, 2001–2007) and Heidelberg (Dr. des., 2008–2013), he held posts at Heidelberg, the University of Vienna, the French Institute of Pondicherry, and the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Boris Aleksandrovich Larin (1893–1964) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv (1910–1914) under Friedrich Knauer and other prominent scholars. He later served as a professor at Saint Petersburg State University.

Boris Ivanovich Klyuev (1927–2000) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University. His career included posts at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the CPSU Central Committee, the Moscow State Institute of International Relations, and the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Boris Ivanovich Pankratov (1892–1979) was a specialist in sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the Eastern Institute, he held positions at Far Eastern Federal University, Harvard-Yenching Institute, the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, Saint Petersburg State University, and the University of Chicago.

Boris Karpushkin (1925–1987) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies (~1946–1951). He worked at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (1961–1974) and taught at MGIMO (1974).

Boris Leonidovič Smirnov (1891–1967) was an Indologist who studied at the S. M. Kirov Military Medical Academy (~1909–1914). He served as director of Turkmen State Medical University (~1935–1956) and was a member of the Academy of Sciences of Turkmenistan (~1951–1967).

Boris Mikhailovich Lyapunov (1862–1943) was a linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vatroslav Jagić and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov. He held academic posts at the University of Kharkiv, Odesa University, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Boris Oguibénine (1940–2025) was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He served as a professor and later professor emeritus at the University of Strasbourg and was a member of EHESS and director/secretary general of the International Association for Comparative Mythology.

Boris Stavisky (1926–2006) specialized in history, archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Saint Petersburg State University and Institute of History, he worked at the Hermitage Museum, the State Museum of Oriental Art, and the Kara-Tepe Archaeological Expedition.

Boris Turayev (1868–1920) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at St. Petersburg University and under Adolf Erman, and he served on the faculty at Saint Petersburg State University from 1896 until his death in 1920.

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov (1900–1981) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky (~1924–1929) and worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1930–1933).

Boris Vladimirovič Semičëv (1900–1984) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy and held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Culture, University of Chicago, Kunstkamera, and the Buryat Institute of Social Sciences.

Boris Vladimirtsov (1884–1931) worked in linguistics, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Antoine Meillet and Paul Pelliot, later holding posts at Saint Petersburg State University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Boris Vsevolodovič Miller (1877–1956) was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. Educated at Moscow State University and the Lazarev Institute, his posts included Moscow State University, the State Museum of Ethnology, and the Institute of Linguistics.
Bortolo Maria Bortolazzi (1806–1879) was an Indologist. He taught Greek at the Ginnasio Comunale di Bassano (1853–1854) and held a post at the Liceo Classico Jacopo Stellini until 1860.
Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima (1898–1959) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Śrī Siṃha Shedra under Thupten Nyendrak, Khenpo Genam, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Boyd Michailovsky is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his PhD from the University of California in 1981. He worked at UC Berkeley, LACITO, and served as Directeur de recherche at the CNRS from 1979 to 2010.
Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Byrski and served as a faculty member at the University of Warsaw around 1993.
